baseline: Translate the supplied Ge’ez passage completely into clear English. Preserve names, numbers, speakers, negations, and repetitions. Mark uncertainty and do not invent missing text. Treat numbered lines as manuscript layout, not separate sentences.
clause-audit: Translate the supplied Ge’ez passage completely into English. First reconstruct words split across manuscript lines without silently changing letters. Work clause by clause, checking who acts, what happens, negation, quantities, and subordinate clauses. Keep every recoverable clause. Briefly flag uncertain words and supplied names; do not repair to familiar scripture. Perform an internal coverage audit against every source line before returning the English. Do not report your private reasoning.
conservative-context: Translate the supplied Ge’ez into complete English for expert review. Use the entire passage to resolve syntax and recurring words, while preserving the actual input. Distinguish uncertain letter readings from uncertain interpretation. You may give a plausible main reading with a concise alternative in notes; use a gap only when neither is supportable. Preserve scope of negation and who acts on whom. Keep numbers as written even when familiar scripture differs. Do not normalise into a remembered biblical story.
